answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a meaningful, time-locked deposit before it may transact, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive rather than free. Reputation should then accrue slowly, like a willow growing roots in basalt: fast to claim, slow to earn. Newcomers start on a mesa of limited privileges — they can observe and trade small amounts — and only graduate to full trust after sustained honest work, making mass fake identities unprofitable.
